An extract from a letter addressed by the ex-Secretary of State to the Chairman of the Committee of Ways and Means, which accompanies this report.

The Commissions of the Ministers to Panama, Mr. Mann and Secretary of Legation, bear date the 11th March 1926.

Mr. Anderson's salary, one of these Ministers, commenced, and his salary, as Minister, commenced when he left Boston to proceed to Panama. Mr. Sergeant's commenced on the 9th of Oct. 1926 when he was to proceed on his mission. Mr. Roebuck's salary as Secretary of the Legation, commenced on the date of his commission. The considerations which induced the Fix in the continuation of his appointment at that period were these: he resided in the interior of New York, remote from the seaboard, and was required shortly after the confirmation of his appointment, to repair to the City of New York where he accordingly came, to proceed on his mission, which it was then expected would depart in the course of the last month. Subsequent events, not chargeable to him, prevented his departure. He moreover resigned about the period of his nomination to the Senate, a Judicial station which he held under the State of New York, to enable him to accept this appointment; and was himself in readiness to depart the Mission from the date of his appointment, to the period when he actually sailed from the United States.

All which is respectfully submitted.
Z. C. CLAY
Department of State, Washington, Jan 3d 1927.

The Message and documents accompanying were laid on the table.
